raw_response:
I have been farming here in Quzhou for 15 years, and I know my land well. My family has 4 people but some of them work in town, so I do not have much extra labor. That means I need to be smart about where I put my effort. Cotton has always been my main crop because the price is usually good and I understand it. This year I will plant cotton on my better plots — about 10.5 mu — and keep 6.4 mu for maize. The maize is partly for our own use and partly to sell, but cotton is where I expect to make most of my money.

For cotton, I will buy improved seed from the dealer in town — I have used varieties like Guoxinmian before and they do well here. I will rotary till the soil before planting in late April because cotton needs a loose seedbed. I will put down compound fertilizer as basal, about 100 jin per mu, and topdress with urea when the plants start flowering. That should give me roughly 22 kg of nitrogen, 9 kg of phosphorus, and 12 kg of potassium per mu. Cotton needs water at key times — emergence, flowering, and boll filling — so I will irrigate 3 times from my well. I cannot waste water because the well has limits. The biggest headache with cotton is pests, especially bollworm. I will spray pesticides about 14 times this season; I know it is a lot, but if I skip sprays I will lose the crop.

For maize, I will plant hybrid seed — Denghai 605 or something similar — in June. Because labor is short and maize does not need as much fussing as cotton, I will use no-tillage planting. It saves me time and fuel. I will apply less fertilizer than cotton, about 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu, mostly as compound fertilizer at sowing. Maize only needs 2 irrigations from the well, and maybe 3 pesticide sprays total — one for weeds and a couple for insects. If the weather is normal, I expect about 550 kg of seed cotton per mu and about 1,100 kg of maize grain per mu.
